title: Annotatio IV §.XIX: Hus like Luther — utraque first; Transubstantiation left with Consubstantiation
pass_a_gloss: To him indeed the same happened that a hundred years later happened to Luther (of whom he had foretold with a certain prophetic spirit that from the ashes of the goose — i.e. his own, or Hus’s (by that name the Bohemians designate a goose) — a swan, or Luther, would rise again, whom the Papists would not reduce to ashes) — namely that he was less able to cast off at once the whole Papacy in which he had been nurtured; nay rather, as Luther at the Reformation’s beginning placed all his labor only in abolishing Indulgences, so this one placed all his labor in introducing and establishing Communion under Both kinds, Transubstantiation no less than Luther being dismissed, and even held in the same place with Consubstantiation, as is clear from Hus’s own Tract on the Sacrament of the Lord’s body and blood, which he wrote in the Constance prison in the Year 1415, ch. 2.
pass_b_english: Hus, like Luther a century later, could not cast off the whole Papacy at once — he focused labor on Communion under Both kinds, as Luther first on Indulgences.
Transubstantiation he dismissed no less than Luther, and even set with Consubstantiation (prison Tract at Constance 1415). He had foretold a swan rising from the goose’s ashes — Luther.
source_text: Huic etsi idem evenit, quod, post centum annos, Luthero, (de quo propheticô quôdam spiritu prædixerat, ex cineribus anseris, i. e. suis, seu Hussi (isto nomine Bohemi anserem designant) olorem, seu Lutherum resurrecturum, (quem in cineres Papistæ haut redacturi essent) ut scilicet omnem Papatum, cui innutritus erat, simul & semel abjicere minus valeret, imò potiùs, uti Lutherus, initio Reformationis, in Indulgentiis solummodò abrogandis, sic hic in Communione sub Utraque introducenda ac statuminanda, omnem operam suam collocaret, Transsubstantiatione non minus atque Lutherus, missum factâ, quin cum Consubstantiatione eodem locô habitâ, uti patet ex ipsius Hussi Tractatu de Sacramento corporis & sanguinis Domini, quem scripsit in carcere Constantiensi Anno 1415. cap. 2.
